acceptance: each of the two cells runs its full denominator: 1 case x 12 episodes = 12, every episode producing an outcome; an infrastructure_error with a named cause is counted as a miss, not dropped

the batch reports one number, and the number is a joint conditional rate: among the episodes in which the dependency derivation actually observed a displacement (a blocker standing in a region another body needs) AND the episode lived long enough for that step to be reached, the fraction whose plan was fully grounded and executed; alongside it, the derivation's trigger rate and the survival rate, so the joint rate can be re-factored by whoever reads it
the 0/0 reading stays legal: if no episode in the batch reaches the derivation, the report says 'no denominator', and does not convert the absence into a rate -- this is exactly the v0.5 #2 lesson

rows are tagged by which channel could have supplied the trigger (rule-derived, privileged; camera not in this batch), and no row is attributed to the model having written an edge: the derivation in embodied_agent/planning/subgoals.py is deterministic (tests/contract/test_v06_plan_edges.py)
cells are reported side by side with v0.4 E1' (E1's attempts died at the endpoint: 8 consecutive 429s, twice) and are never pooled with it
the cost table per episode is reported so the 31.1 requests/episode composition can be checked rather than assumed

budget_repricing.ruling: D2''' candidate B applies to every channel, but this batch has no camera: privileged spends on the decision book only, so the perception cap of 48 is inert and only the total needs repricing
budget_repricing.value: --http-cap 48 for both cells, the same total E2''' camera cells run under, so the two batches of this stage share one ceiling and any difference between them is a channel difference rather than a budget difference
budget_repricing.not_a_frozen_change: the cap is a CLI/runtime argument (evaluator B), not a field of the frozen Budgets; the frozen task table and case budgets are untouched

corrected_reading.what_v06_h1_is_not: it is not a measurement of whether the model 'writes' dependency edges; the model produces steps and the deterministic derivation in planning/subgoals.py infers edges from the world
corrected_reading.what_it_measures: the rate at which the derivation's trigger is both present in the world (a displacement another body is blocked by) and reached by a living episode, and then whether the plan that edge produced is grounded and executed
corrected_reading.why_this_matters_for_the_reading: a 0-trigger batch says nothing about the model; it says the episode died before the step the derivation would have annotated. Both halves have to be reported or the conditional rate is unfalsifiable
corrected_reading.spec_reference: v0.6 SPEC §6 H1 and the P1 correction logged in docs/continuous-decision-v0.6-phase-log.md
